newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, gold at 20 month low.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, gold at 20 month low.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Thursday, led by a gold market which slid to its lowest levels since March 1995 under the weight of producer hedging and fund selling, traders said.

"Some selling from South Africa gave some cover to the shorts who now feel they have a free ride, what with talk of central bank selling still hanging over the market," Chase Manhattan managing director, Dinsa Mehta said.
The price of gold in Australian dollar terms and in South African rand has fallen sharply this week, encouraging producer hedging from those countries, traders said.
COMEX December gold ended down $2.50 an ounce at $376.50, after breaching the October 31 contract low at $377.80 and falling to a new life-of-contract low at $375.80.

Spot gold in the bullion market closed quoted $376.30/376.80, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $377.00, its lowest fix since March 1995, and compared to the New York close Wednesday around $378.20/378.80.

"Gold is continuing to erode away in a very slow but steady fashion with most bullion dealers looking for $370 basis spot as a downside target before the end of the year," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.

The jump in the Australian dollar overnight to US$0.81 resulted in the price of gold in Australian dollars falling to to around A$464.00 from around $480 an ounce earlier this week, prompting hedge selling from Australian producers, traders said.

Meanwhile, the partial recovery in the South African rand this week, pushed down the price of gold in rand also to around 1725 rand, from a multi-year high around 1800 rand in early November, encouraging South African producers to try to lock in some gains, analysts said.

On the daily charts, December gold has been in a long downtrend from the five year highs at $417 seen in February this year, but Thursday's close resulted in a nine-day relative strength indicator (RSI) reading of only 28 percent suggesting the current downswing may be getting oversold.
With both December gold and silver entering the delivery period on November 27, rollover activity has also contributed to volumes this week.

December gold open interest fell another 2,058 lots Wednesday, while February's rose 2,490, but total COMEX gold open interest has fallen sharply in the past 10 days from 196,754 on November 8, to 175,954 on November 19, suggesting funds have been covering some short positions, traders said.
The December/February gold spread ended around $2.20 an ounce Thursday, after narrowing steadily from around $2.80 in July this year.
Meanwhile gold's fundamentals remain weak, analysts said.
The sharp rise in the U.S. dollar in the past year to 42 month highs against the yen early this month, has constrained Asian demand.

World gold demand in the 10 largest gold consuming markets slipped to 1,566 tonnes in the first nine months of 1996, four percent below the record levels in the same period last year, the World Gold Council said Wednesday.
COMEX December silver ended down 10.5 cent at $4.840 an ounce, after trading down to a 12 day low at $4.805.
Spot silver, which traded down to $4.82 Thursday, has been in a downtrend since May 1995 when five year highs were seen around $6.14 an ounce.
NYMEX January platinum closed down 90 cents at $387.30 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium lost 45 cents to end of at $119.00.
But the April platinum/gold spread jumped to $9.40 an ounce by the close, from $7.70 at Wednesday's close, continuing its recovery from late October.
-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
